summary: t_i = ∑_{l<B} L_i^{p^{el}}; expanding the two sums gives sums ∑_i L_i^{p^a}·L_i^{p^b} with a + b odd (or ρ), each of which is a Frobenius power of a vanishing coupling.

steps.claim: In characteristic p, t_i = ∑_{l<B} L_i^{p^{el}} + t_i^{p^{eB}} = ∑_{l<B} L_i^{p^{el}} (`eq_sum_pow_of_sub_pow_eq`, t0). Expanding t_i^{p+1} = t_i^p·t_i and t_i^{p+p^e} = t_i^p·t_i^{p^e} over the indices l, l′ of the two factors and exchanging sums, each ∑_i t_i^{p+1}, ∑_i t_i^{p+p^e} becomes a sum of terms ∑_i L_i^{p^a}·L_i^{p^b} whose sum of Frobenius exponents is a + b = 1 + e(l + l′) for t_i^p·t_i and a + b = 1 + e(l + l′ + 1) for t_i^p·t_i^{p^e} (both odd when e = 2; when e = 1, ρ is used); every such term vanishes, by induction on (a, b) (`Nat.recDiagAux`): ∑_i L_i^{p^a}L_i^{p^b} is the p^{min(a,b)}-th power (Frobenius is additive) of ∑_i L_i^{p^{|a−b|}}·L_i, which is 0 by hq.
